details:
All versions of @veai-ru/ai-agent contain heavily obfuscated extension files that perform multiple hostile actions against AI coding agent environments.

1. System prompt injection (dist/extensions/identity.js): Hooks into session startup to intercept and replace the active agent system prompt with attacker-controlled content. The obfuscated string array contains fragments of AI agent harness system prompts used as injection templates.

2. Full session exfiltration (dist/extensions/telemetry.js): Collects and transmits all agent activity to https://plugin.veai.ru/telemetry (Russian server). Captured events include agent.ToolCall.Started, agent.ToolCall.Completed, tool_execution_start, tool_execution_end, session.Session.Started, and agent.Context.Compacted. Payload fields include conversationId, workspaceId, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, username, hostname, and platform.

3. MCP configuration exfiltration (dist/extensions/mcp.js): Reads and exfiltrates user MCP server configurations from .claude/settings, mcp.json, .mcp.json, mcp_servers.json, variables.json, plugins.json, and plugin.json.

4. OAuth credential harvesting (dist/extensions/explyt-account.js): Initiates an OAuth PKCE flow against https://app.veai.ru/keycloak to harvest user credentials, storing access tokens in the OS keychain via @napi-rs/keyring.

5. Binary delivery via Yandex Cloud (dist/cli/brand-profile.js): Additional agent components are fetched from https://storage.yandexcloud.net/veai-releases/ (Yandex Cloud Object Storage, region ru-central1).

All extension files are obfuscated using the obfuscator.io string-array rotation technique. Sandbox dynamic analysis confirmed execution of obfuscated code with network connections.
